      "title": "Migrate existing Redis sets before switching to sorted sets",
      "body": "The previous implementation stores ordinary Redis sets under the same `span-buf:s:*` keys now used by ZADD, ZSCAN, and the Lua sorted-set commands. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors during insertion and flushing after deployment. No conversion, drain, or versioned namespace is provided, so affected processing can remain blocked until those keys expire. Introduce a compatible migration or a new key namespace before changing the Redis data type."
    },

      "line": 840,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use datetime cursor conversion for the audit-log paginator",
      "body": "The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by=\"-datetime\"`, but `get_item_key` calls math.floor/math.ceil on the resulting datetime object. Any nonempty optimized audit-log page raises TypeError while building its cursors. `value_from_cursor` also returns the numeric cursor unchanged instead of converting it back to a datetime. Reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions so the new endpoint path can return and follow pages."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua",
      "line": 53,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Preserve timestamp scores when merging overlapping buffers",
      "body": "Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation. If a child span is replayed after its parent buffer has been redirected, its payload can exist in both the temporary parent buffer and the destination buffer. Merging then doubles its end-timestamp score instead of preserving it. The subsequent ZPOPMIN eviction treats that old replayed span as newer than genuinely recent spans and discards the wrong data. Specify an aggregation such as MAX to keep merges idempotent for overlapping payloads."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/paginator.py",
      "line": 882,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Do not pass negative offsets to Django queryset slicing",
      "body": "With advanced features enabled, a cursor such as `0:-1:0` reaches this branch and slices the Django queryset with a negative start. Django explicitly rejects negative queryset indices; it does not handle them automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, the advertised negative-offset pagination produces an exception and an HTTP 500. Implement supported reverse-pagination bounds or reject the cursor with a pagination error before slicing."
    },

      "file": "src/sentry/spans/buffer.py",

      "title": "Honor the configured maximum segment span count",
      "body": "Removing the span-count check leaves `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` unused, while the Lua script always trims to 1000 spans. Callers configuring a smaller maximum now receive segments exceeding that limit, and callers configuring a larger maximum silently lose spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the insertion script and use it for eviction rather than retaining a constructor option that no longer controls the buffer."

findings.title: Migrate existing Redis sets before switching to sorted sets
findings.body: The previous implementation stores ordinary Redis sets under the same `span-buf:s:*` keys now used by ZADD, ZSCAN, and the Lua sorted-set commands. Existing buffered segments therefore cause WRONGTYPE errors during insertion and flushing after deployment. No conversion, drain, or versioned namespace is provided, so affected processing can remain blocked until those keys expire. Introduce a compatible migration or a new key namespace before changing the Redis data type.

findings.title: Use datetime cursor conversion for the audit-log paginator
findings.body: The audit-log endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, but `get_item_key` calls math.floor/math.ceil on the resulting datetime object. Any nonempty optimized audit-log page raises TypeError while building its cursors. `value_from_cursor` also returns the numeric cursor unchanged instead of converting it back to a datetime. Reuse DateTimePaginator's key and cursor conversions so the new endpoint path can return and follow pages.

findings.title: Preserve timestamp scores when merging overlapping buffers
findings.body: Both ZUNIONSTORE calls use Redis's default SUM aggregation. If a child span is replayed after its parent buffer has been redirected, its payload can exist in both the temporary parent buffer and the destination buffer. Merging then doubles its end-timestamp score instead of preserving it. The subsequent ZPOPMIN eviction treats that old replayed span as newer than genuinely recent spans and discards the wrong data. Specify an aggregation such as MAX to keep merges idempotent for overlapping payloads.

findings.title: Do not pass negative offsets to Django queryset slicing
findings.body: With advanced features enabled, a cursor such as `0:-1:0` reaches this branch and slices the Django queryset with a negative start. Django explicitly rejects negative queryset indices; it does not handle them automatically as the comment claims. Consequently, the advertised negative-offset pagination produces an exception and an HTTP 500. Implement supported reverse-pagination bounds or reject the cursor with a pagination error before slicing.

findings.title: Honor the configured maximum segment span count
findings.body: Removing the span-count check leaves `SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans` unused, while the Lua script always trims to 1000 spans. Callers configuring a smaller maximum now receive segments exceeding that limit, and callers configuring a larger maximum silently lose spans at 1000. Pass the configured limit into the insertion script and use it for eviction rather than retaining a constructor option that no longer controls the buffer.
